thought: Created two Linux VRF devices on r1 using tables 10 and 20, then attached eth1/eth3 to vrf-blue and eth2/eth4 to vrf-red as requested. Assigned gateway IPs on the tenant and shared links and ensured IPv4 forwarding is enabled on r1. On the tenant hosts, removed the incorrect cross-tenant next-hop behavior by installing routes that send only their own shared-service segment to the correct r1 gateway, while any route toward the other tenant/subnet also resolves to the local VRF gateway so traffic remains confined to the local VRF path. Management on eth0 was left untouched.
